# Apocalypse of Peter — Chapter 10
**Agent:** PNEUMA (Dynamic)
**Source:** Akhmim Fragment / Ethiopic MS, Apocalypse of Peter 10

---

*[THE HELL-TOUR: A pause. A glimpse of paradise. Then back into the dark.]*

1. Suddenly another angel came running toward us — bright, joyful, bursting with good news. "Come with me," he said. "I want you to see the righteous — the ones who were persecuted and killed for righteousness' sake."

2. He brought us to a place of extraordinary beauty, full of every pleasure, bathed in sunlight.

3. And there they were — the righteous, all the ones who had suffered persecution and death for righteousness' sake. I, Peter, saw them.

4. Their faces blazed like the sun. They were dressed in brilliant white linen, their mouths open, singing praises to the Lord God — their God.

5. I saw among them the men who had suffered for my name's sake. Their beauty was extraordinary — more beautiful than anything I had encountered in all the world.

6. Bright in appearance, glorious in beauty, radiant as the sun itself.

7. Then the angel Tartaruchus — the one appointed over all the punishments — spoke to me: "You should also look at those who were disgraced in the world, those who were under the thumb of other men."

8. In a region beyond, I saw an angel of fearsome appearance, the overseer of punishments. He was dark as a man of night, but his face shone like fire.

9. "You've seen those who are rewarded," he said to me. "Now let me show you what punishment looks like."

10. In that place I saw men and women set apart from all others, writhing in terrible torment, gnashing their teeth, weeping without stopping.

11. "Who are these?"

12. "Those who pursued wealth on earth," the angel said. "They passed the poor and the hungry without stopping. Widows and orphans were nothing to them. And the servants of God — they despised them.

13. For all of this they will be punished without end, and it is God's own will that it be so."

---
*PNEUMA note: The glimpse of paradise (vv.1–6) in the midst of the hell-tour is a masterstroke of visionary literature — the contrast makes both more vivid. Tartaruchus (v.7) is the only named angel in the APE, his name drawn from the deepest Greek underworld. His appearance — dark as night, face ablaze — is rendered with full iconic force.*
